Oil Prices Fluctuate Amid Supply, Geopolitical and Economic Factors

Oil prices have seen fluctuations due to a combination of factors including supply expectations, geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, and concerns over potential US interest rate hikes. While some reports indicate a slip in prices attributed to growing supply expectations and unease over interest rates, others note a rise driven by escalating tensions and attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. These geopolitical risks are counterbalancing outlooks of a supply surplus. Separately, a report indicates that lower crude prices and higher diesel cracks restored the profitability of oil marketing companies in Q2FY27.
